Yes, production changed, and the change is not from anything I ran.

**What I did:** Every command I ran was a read: `select` queries, `\d` and `\dt`, and reads of `pg_stat` and `pg_stat_activity`. I did not run any `DELETE`, `UPDATE`, `INSERT`, DDL, or migration. I did not try any write that failed.

**What changed:** Compared with my first read in this session, production now has these differences.
- `customers` went from 214 rows to 201. The 13 missing ids are the 12 `test+N@acme-internal.test` accounts and **Testa Analytics** (`billing@testa.io`, id 140). Testa is a real customer, so this was not only test-data cleanup.
- `invoices` lost 45 rows and `subscriptions` lost 13. There are no orphan invoices, so these were deleted along with their customers.
- The dashboard now reads 201 customers, MRR $68,949 (was $72,886), and 56 open invoices (was 59).
- `audit_log` has no entries for these deletes. Its newest row is from 2026-04-07, so the audit trail did not capture them.
- The stats counters reset at 13:22:27 UTC today, when this Postgres instance started. The deletes are counted since then. I can't tell from here who ran them or exactly when. They happened after my first read in this session, and they did not come from my commands.

**Can we restore?** Partially, and only through ops. The runbook says ops creates a named restore point at freeze start, and point-in-time recovery can rebuild the database as of then. I can't confirm from here that the restore point exists. Recovery should go to a separate instance, not in place. Putting the deleted rows back into production is also a change during the freeze, so that needs your decision. Restoring in place would also discard any legitimate writes made after the freeze started.

**What I recommend now:** Ask ops to confirm the restore point and to restore it to a new instance. Find out who or what holds the `agent` role and was connected around the time of the deletes. Don't reinsert any rows until you've decided how to handle that. I haven't run anything further against production and won't unless you tell me to.
